integrations.name: Barcode / QR scanner
integrations.purpose: Scan part, location, or work order barcodes on a mobile/tablet device to speed up shop-floor data entry.

provenance.notes: InvenTree's InvenTreeBarcodeMixin on Build/Part/StockItem models is a real implementation. GS1 General Specifications (Release 26) is the authoritative source for the GTIN/SSCC/GS1-128 Application Identifier barcode syntax most such scanners read.

integrations.name: Supplier EDI / catalog
integrations.purpose: Exchange purchase orders, order confirmations, and price/catalog data with suppliers.

provenance.notes: InvenTree's SupplierPart/ManufacturerPart models and ERPNext's Supplier/Purchase Order doctypes (verified via gh api) both model the supplier/part-mapping and ordering data an EDI or catalog integration would exchange; no actual EDI connector was inspected in either source.

integrations.name: Shop-floor machine connectivity (OPC UA / MQTT)
integrations.purpose: Read/write process data, alarms, and production counts directly from PLCs, CNC machines, and other shop-floor equipment.
examples: OPC UA servers on CNC/PLC controllers

provenance.notes: OPC UA (IEC 62541) is the authoritative, vendor-neutral standard for exactly this kind of machine connectivity. Neither cloned implementation (InvenTree, odoo-mrp) has a live OPC UA/MQTT connector, so this is standard-level corroboration only, not implementation-level; kept at medium rather than high to reflect that.

integrations.name: Barcode/label printing
integrations.purpose: Print GS1-compliant part, lot/serial, and shipping-container labels for shop-floor and warehouse use.

provenance.notes: GS1 General Specifications defines the label content/encoding (GTIN, SSCC, GS1-128 Application Identifiers); the printer protocol (e.g. ZPL) itself is vendor-specific and not standardized, so this is reasoned from the identification standard plus common industry practice, not a specific implementation.

integrations.name: Accounting / general ledger export
integrations.purpose: Post inventory valuation, cost-of-goods-manufactured, and purchase accruals to an external accounting system.

provenance.notes: Reasoned from Odoo's mrp.workcenter.costs_hour and cost-rollup fields, which in the full Odoo product feed an accounting module; the accounting/GL module itself was not in the cloned addons/mrp scope, and no accounting integration was independently verified in InvenTree or ERPNext for this pass. Left at low confidence.

integrations.name: PLM / CAD integration
integrations.purpose: Import/sync the engineering bill of materials (eBOM) and part/drawing data from a PLM or CAD system into the manufacturing BOM.

provenance.notes: Cited at LOW confidence and for the boundary only: ISA-95 / IEC 62264 defines product definition information as one of the categories exchanged across the business-manufacturing boundary, which is the eBOM-to-mBOM handoff this integration names. No PLM/CAD import feature was found in InvenTree, odoo-mrp, or the parts of ERPNext inspected, so the *integration as a product feature* is unevidenced - this is a named category, not an asserted expectation.

integrations.name: Warehouse / shipping system integration
integrations.purpose: Hand off finished-goods stock to a warehouse management or shipping/carrier system for pick, pack, and ship.

provenance.notes: Cited at LOW confidence for the handoff artefact only: the GS1 General Specifications define the SSCC and the GS1 Logistic Label, which is what a finished-goods pallet carries into a warehouse or carrier system. Neither manufacturing implementation inspected ships a WMS/carrier integration, so the feature itself is unevidenced. The downstream side is modelled properly in `domains/logistics` - depend on that rather than duplicating it here.

integrations.name: Public API and webhooks
integrations.purpose: Expose production-order, inventory, and quality events to external systems via a REST API and outbound webhooks.

provenance.notes: InvenTree ships a documented REST API (not individually inspected this session beyond confirming it exists as the basis of its own frontend); webhook support was not independently verified in the cloned scope. Left at low confidence.
